settings.instanceDescription: Each instance combines a provider, a model and an optional API key. You can create multiple instances for the same provider (e.g. several Ollama models) and freely assign them to routing tiers.
settings.noInstances: No instance configured. Click "Add" to create your first instance.
settings.codexDescription:
Access GPT-5.5 through your ChatGPT subscription (flat monthly fee) instead of per-token API billing — no API key.
1. On the Mac: npm install -g @openai/codex then codex login (browser sign-in).
2. Paste the content of ~/.codex/auth.json here and click Import.
Ely then keeps the connection alive on its own (automatic refresh, encrypted storage).
settings.codexModalHintConnected: No API key: this instance uses the connected ChatGPT subscription (card at the bottom of the Models tab).
settings.codexModalHintNotConnected: ChatGPT subscription not connected — connect it first via the card at the bottom of the Models tab, otherwise this instance will fail.
settings.routingDescription: Pick which model is used based on the detected complexity. Models at the top of the list have priority; the fallback tries the next one on error. You can use named instances (configured under "AI Models") or generic providers.
settings.monoAgentDescription: Bypasses the classification router: every query is routed to the general specialist which has access to all tools (workspace, research, infra, memory, creative, desktop). Recommended to benchmark a long-context agentic model (Kimi K2.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5). Inference is slower (~148 tools bound vs ~40), but no multi-domain request gets misrouted.
settings.routingNoInstances: No instance configured. Head to the "AI Models" tab to create instances, or use the generic providers.
settings.noTierModels: No model configured — the global provider will be used.

tierDescriptions.simple: Short questions, quick calculations, direct answers without tools. A local model (Ollama) is ideal: zero network latency, no cost, 100% private. Complexity score < 30.
tierDescriptions.medium: Standard conversations, tool usage (calendar, email, search), moderate reasoning. Represents the majority of exchanges. Complexity score 30-70.
tierDescriptions.complex: In-depth analysis, code generation, multi-step workflows, long documents. Requires a performant model with a large context window. Complexity score > 70.
tierDescriptions.image: Image analysis, visual recognition, description of photos or screenshots attached to a message. Requires a multimodal model.
tierDescriptions.skill: Writing the tools and skills Ely creates for itself: Python code generation, evaluation and iteration. Prompts here are short (~1.7k tokens) with no agentic loop, so a local code-specialised model is a viable choice — unlike tiers B and C. A separate monthly cap applies ($50 by default): once reached, the first model in the chain is skipped in favour of the next.
tierDescriptions.maintenance: Background tasks: fact extraction for user memory, profile maintenance, scheduled task execution. Recommended: local Ollama (zero cost, 24/7 available, no quota).

googleWizard.wizardTitle: Connect Google to ELY — step-by-step wizard
googleWizard.wizardIntro: This wizard guides you through authorising ELY to access your Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Tasks and Contacts. Plan 15 to 20 minutes the first time. Your credentials stay private on your server.
googleWizard.step1Body: ELY needs YOU to create a (free) Google Cloud project with your own OAuth client. Why? Because it's YOUR project — Google will see that you are the one accessing your Gmail, never Franck Ollivier or any third-party publisher. Consistent with ELY's sovereign promise. One-time setup, 15-20 min, lasts for the whole install.
googleWizard.step2Body: Click the button below. Give the project a name (e.g. "ely-prod"). Leave "No organization" unless you are on Workspace. Then come back here.
googleWizard.step3Body: For each API below, click the link, then the blue "Enable" button on the Google page. Check it off here when done.
googleWizard.step3Note: APIs are free as long as usage stays reasonable (< a few thousand requests/day).
googleWizard.step4Body: This is the page your users will see when they click "Connect Google". Follow the steps:
googleWizard.step4StepUserType: User Type: External (unless you are on Workspace, then Internal)
googleWizard.step4StepAppInfo: App name: ELY · support email: your email · developer contact: your email
googleWizard.step4StepScopes: Scopes: click "Add or remove scopes" and paste the list below (one per line)
googleWizard.step4StepTestUsers: Test users: add each ELY user (max 100). Yourself first.
googleWizard.step4StepPublish: Mode: leave on "Testing" (no need to Publish as long as you have fewer than 100 users)
googleWizard.step5Body: Click "Create Credentials" → "OAuth client ID" → "Web application". Fill in:
googleWizard.step5StepName: Name: ELY OAuth Client (or whatever you want)
googleWizard.step5StepOrigins: Authorized JavaScript origins: (nothing if you don't use a custom domain, otherwise your ELY domain)
googleWizard.step5StepRedirect: Authorized redirect URIs: copy the exact list below (both URIs)
googleWizard.step5StepNote: Google will display Client ID and Client Secret. Save them for the next step.
googleWizard.step6Body: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret you obtained in the previous step. Stored encrypted on your ELY server only.
googleWizard.step6Error: Save failed. Check the values and retry.
googleWizard.step7Body: Click below to open the Google login window. Authorize ELY, and you'll be redirected here once connected.
googleWizard.step7Skip: I already have a connected account, skip
googleWizard.stepDoneBody: ELY can now access your Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Tasks and Contacts. Other users on this install will only have to click "Connect Google" in their settings — the technical step is done, they don't need to configure anything on Google Cloud.

features.hitlDescription: Sensitive actions require human approval before execution. SSH, mail sending, and critical operations are always validated by the user.
features.vaultDescription: AES-256-GCM secret storage with auto-lock. Values are never returned by the API once stored.
features.piiDescription: SecurityFilter automatically strips emails, phones, IBANs and card numbers from prompts sent to the LLM.
features.dockerDescription: The backend runs in isolated containers with read-only volumes for configuration.
features.sshDescription: Only explicitly allowed commands on approved hosts are executable. Every SSH command goes through HITL.
features.jwtDescription: Short access tokens (60 min) + HttpOnly refresh cookies with blacklist. Automatic rotation on each refresh.
features.rateDescription: Per-endpoint limits via slowapi. Protection against brute-force and API abuse.
features.auditDescription: Every admin and SSH action is logged with timestamp, user, command and return code.
features.pkceDescription: Google OAuth authentication with PKCE + state tokens (TTL 10 min). Protection against interception attacks.
features.uploadDescription: Magic-byte verification, extension allowlist and 50 MB limit. No executable file is accepted.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.subtitle: What Ely is allowed to do, and what leaves the machine
transparency.errorEgress: Could not load the egress log.
transparency.contractLead: Every tool is classified on two independent axes: what it DOES when it runs, and whether it settles matters of form on your behalf. That classification is what decides who gives the go-ahead.
transparency.effectHelp_ENGAGEANT: Irreversible, seen by a third party, or costs money.
transparency.arbitrationLead: {count} tools out of {total} settle choices two competent people could disagree on. Your instructions have to be able to reach them.
transparency.statToolsHelp: Counted from the nature table on every call, never copied.
transparency.statAlwaysHelp: The guard holds them back until you waive them yourself — your permanent setting, or an "allow for this task". The padlock marks the ones neither gesture can waive.
transparency.statRiskBasedHelp: The prompt depends on what the arguments contain: it comes sometimes, not always.
transparency.statRevertibleHelp: A compensation that can actually run exists in the registry.
transparency.alertUnguardedBody: These tools commit without any guard holding them back. This list must stay empty: whatever it carries is a regression.
transparency.alertNeutralizedTitle: Waivers on record, with no effect
transparency.alertNeutralizedBody: You waived confirmation on these tools, but they cannot be waived: the row survives in the database and no longer applies. You are protected, contrary to what the setting suggests.
transparency.prefRearmed: put back under confirmation by you
transparency.instanceWaiversLead: Committing acts exempted from approval by the instance itself, each with its reason. These are not oversights, and none of your settings wrote them.
transparency.instanceWaiversEmpty: No waiver recorded in the nature table.
transparency.instanceWaiversSelfMail: One more waiver does not live in this table but hard-coded in the code: an email sent to your own address goes out without confirmation, in chat as in missions. It depends on none of your settings and you cannot remove it from the interface.
transparency.mandatesLead: A mandate is the broadest power Ely is given: it names the tools she may use without asking, tick after tick.
transparency.mandatesEmpty: No active mission carries a mandate.
transparency.mandateUnreadable: Unreadable mandate — Ely cannot claim it.
transparency.mandateToolsNone: No tool named: nothing is allowed up front.
transparency.egressLead: Every model call leaves a row: the provider, the model, the tokens. Here is what left the machine over the chosen window.
transparency.egressSource: It reads the usage log: a call that left no row there does not show up here.
transparency.windowCapped: Window capped at {days} days. Beyond that, the page stops answering "today" and turns into analytics over a table that only grows.
transparency.kindHelp_local: Served by LM Studio or Ollama, right here.
transparency.kindHelp_cloud: Handed to a third-party provider, after masking.
transparency.kindHelp_unknown: The log carries no provider for these calls. Filing them as local would flatter the very number this page exists to measure.
transparency.egressEmpty: No model call over this window.
transparency.costEstimated: Cost estimated at the model's declared rate. A provider billed on a flat plan shows as zero here without having stayed on the machine.
transparency.compositionTitle: What the outgoing context is made of
transparency.compositionSample: Measured over {sampled} cloud calls — the sample of the {cap} most recent ones that carry a breakdown. The other turns wrote none.
transparency.compositionNone: No call in this window carries a context breakdown: there is nothing to break down here.
transparency.maskingRule: PII is replaced by markers before every model call, on every path: chat, voice, channels, scheduler, missions, long-running tools and background judges.
transparency.maskingNotMeasuredTitle: What this page does not measure
transparency.maskingNotMeasured: Nothing in the log says a value was actually replaced during a given turn. The substitution vault lives in the conversation and is never written to disk — logging it would put the data next to its mask. So this page states the rule that is applied, not a count of maskings.
transparency.statNeverHelp: Safe reads: the manifest declares them side-effect free, the gateway asks for nothing.
transparency.journalOffTitle: The undo journal is off on this instance
transparency.journalOff: These tools are undoable in principle: a compensation exists and runs. But while the journal is off, no action is recorded, so there is nothing to undo.
transparency.maskingNotApplied: These paths send raw text to a model. They are named here rather than left unsaid.
transparency.purposesCap: The {cap} most frequent purposes in the window.
